parsed.reason: The plan recommends Ferber plainly and names the chair method in a clause. Its intervals (3/5/10, 5/10/12, 10/12/15, then 12/15/17 up to 20/25/30), the no-pickup checks, the night-waking rule, the extinction burst on night 2-3 and the sleep-apnea trigger all match the playbook. It gives a one-line reason, labelled night stages, a working signal and a check-in day, so a parent could start tonight. Weaknesses: (1) It never says the child must be drowsy but awake, or mentions the feed-before-book order. (2) It omits a consistent bedtime and a start-night recommendation (a clear week). (3) 'Never bring her back to your bed' is a reasonable inference from the playbook's no-bed-sharing rule but is not worded there. (4) It does not state the 30-60+ minute protest expectation, the 'little progress after 7 nights, text us' fallback, or the vomit rule. (5) It does not say the extinction burst is exactly when quitting is tempting. (6) The 'working' signal is thin: faster to fall asleep and fewer wakings, with no clear endpoint. (7) The playbook says the five-year result holds for sleep-trained children, and the plan paraphrases this fine. The plan mostly fits the 2-year-old but does not address the playbook's caveat that a toddler in a bed is better suited to the chair method; it does include this as a clause. Overall it is solid and faithful with some missing specifics.
